prompt: What is this call mainly about?
about: The MCQ ontology as a tree. The root question picks the subject of the call; it does not decide the verdict, because scam and legitimate calls occur under every subject. Every call then answers the common questions and the questions of its subject, and some answers open follow-up questions that are asked only when that answer is chosen. Every answer has a value between -1 and 1: positive points toward scam, negative toward legitimate. The call's score is the sum of the values of the answers chosen.

built_from.previous_version: knowledge/mcq_ontology.json at commit 3ecabb2: six subjects with two levels of questions. Its questions are kept here and extended.

datasets.note: eight call types of 200 calls each; every type is all scam or all legitimate, so the type alone would give the label away
real technical-support scam calls and legitimate support conversations
99 topics, nearly all with one real scam call and one legitimate call written to match, so the subject alone never decides
calls to a honeypot; its non-scam calls are labelled spam, so a sign found about equally often in both classes marks unwanted calls, not scams
scam types of the pooled robocall and scam sets

built_from.evidence_format: Each evidence entry counts the calls labelled scam and nonscam in a dataset that carry a value. In scamai_full_1000 the nonscam calls are spam; elsewhere they are legitimate calls. The counts are read from the CSV files by the script that wrote this file.

how_to_ask.route: Ask the root question first. It is only about the subject of the call, not about whether it is a scam.
how_to_ask.questions: Then ask the common questions and the questions of the chosen subject. Choose exactly one option for each question.
how_to_ask.order: Options run from the strongest scam sign to the strongest legitimate sign, with not_mentioned last. When several options fit, choose the first one that fits.
how_to_ask.follow_up: When the chosen option has follow_up questions, ask them as well. A follow-up is asked only when its option was chosen.
how_to_ask.quotes: Every answer needs a short verbatim quote from the transcript that supports it, except not_mentioned and options marked absence. An answer without a supporting quote counts as not_mentioned.
how_to_ask.absence: Options marked absence say that something did not happen, such as no payment. There is nothing to quote, so they need no quote. Choose one only when the transcript covers the part of the call where it would have happened; for a call cut off early, answer not_mentioned.
how_to_ask.retrieval: After routing, the subject's knowledge entries can be retrieved and shown to the model as context with its questions: the scam_patterns.json patterns and the scam_ontology.json nodes listed under knowledge.
how_to_ask.sequence: Each subject's ask list is the order its calls are asked: urgency first, then the subject's own questions (for a bank call, whether money is to go to a different account), then the other common questions, and the recorded questions last. A follow-up comes straight after the answer that opens it. The call's score is the sum of the values of every answer chosen on the way.

options.text: A recorded message that asks the person to press a key, or to call a number, to speak to someone

common_questions.prompt: How did this conversation come about?

options.text: The person is calling a number shown in a pop-up, a locked or warning screen, or an unexpected email, invoice, or text
options.note: In the YouTube scam-baiting calls the person often rings the scammer from a fake warning or a fake invoice. The matching legitimate calls point out that a real system message never shows a number or a web address (scambait_synthetic_196, topic blocked_message_read_out).

options.text: The caller contacted the person out of the blue about a problem the person did not know about, such as a virus, a charge, a debt, or a legal case
The person is returning a missed call or a voicemail, with no letter or reference to check it against
options.note: The legitimate calls of scambait_synthetic_196 topics tax_office_return_call and customs_callback start by asking for the reference on a letter; the scam calls do not.

options.text: The person called the organisation on a number from its own website, a card, a bill, or a letter, about a problem they noticed themselves

scoring.formula: score = the sum of the values of every chosen option: the common questions, the subject's questions, and every follow-up that was asked
scoring.values: Each value is between -1 and 1. Positive points toward scam and negative toward legitimate; 1.0 is a strong sign and smaller numbers are weaker ones. not_mentioned is always 0.
scoring.recorded: Questions with role recorded score 0 on every option. They record who the caller claims to be or what the call is about, so the verdict can be explained. On their own they separate nothing, because a real bank also says it is a bank.
scoring.tuning: The values are starting points, set from the knowledge files and the evidence in this file. Training on a dataset adds options and updates the values; train on training folds only, never on test calls.

bands_note: The sign of the score decides: above 0 is scam, below 0 is legitimate, and exactly 0 is neutral.
